endorsements.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for AI-Enabled Device Software Functions (final guidance)
endorsements.quote: When implementing a modification to a device with an authorized PCCP, a manufacturer should first consider whether the particular modification is or is not consistent with the authorized PCCP.

commentary.bottom_line: Two FDA guidance documents direct manufacturers to confirm that a modification falls within the authorized predetermined change control plan (PCCP) and follows its methods and specifications before implementation, and one ties this to the design-change requirement in 21 CFR 820.30(i). No study has tested whether this pre-implementation check prevents out-of-scope or nonconforming changes, and no study documents how often such deviations occur.

perspectives.view: The evidence base for this recommendation contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The recommendation rests on regulatory expectation rather than on measured effects on deviation rates or patient outcomes.

The draft lifecycle guidance treats this verification as a mandatory design-control step under 21 CFR 820.30(i), which requires procedures to identify, document, validate or verify, review, and approve design changes before implementation. The final PCCP guidance uses advisory language and asks manufacturers to first consider whether a modification is consistent with the authorized plan.

commentary.research_gap: No study has measured how often manufacturers implement AI device modifications that fall outside an authorized PCCP or depart from its methods and performance specifications. No study has compared deviation rates, recall rates, or post-change performance between manufacturers with and without a formal pre-implementation consistency check. Reviews of FDA inspection findings or postmarket reports for PCCP-authorized devices could supply a first estimate of how often the hazard occurs.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested this practice, so no evidence exists for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether a change that stays within an authorized plan preserves performance for these groups may depend on whether the plan's performance specifications include subgroup criteria, which this recommendation does not address.
